articleBlocks: Username, Plea, and Contest all suggest different kinds of entry, but they can still feel like a paperwork board rather than a clean category. The opening clues stay ambiguous until Building (through a doorway) gives the board a cleaner test, so this guide starts with the misleading first read, then uses the later clues to show why the final connection is narrower than the early guesses and how each clue checks that same pattern without relying on the answer reveal too early.
Spreadsheet item keeps the verb enter in play, especially if you think about data entry.
Building (through a doorway) is the clue that proves the idea is much broader.
Once physical movement joins legal forms, account fields, and competitions, the answer stops being about one system and becomes Things you enter.
The answer was Things you enter.
This board is satisfying because the same verb works across digital, legal, competitive, and physical contexts.
solutionNarrative: Username and Spreadsheet item made the board feel like something about forms or typed inputs, while Plea and Contest kept nudging the same verb into other settings. That helped, but it still felt narrower than the real category.
Building (through a doorway) solved the ambiguity. Once physical movement joined the set, enter became the only verb broad enough to explain every clue cleanly.

lessons.title: Broad verbs can hide inside narrow-looking systems
